### 2.1 Domain, Range & Composite Functions (Domain & Range)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **20 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Determination of real domain and range, floor and fractional part functions, and domain constraints on composite functions.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{For } \sqrt{f(x)} \implies f(x) \ge 0, \quad \text{For } \log_b(f(x)) \implies f(x) > 0, b > 0, b \ne 1, \quad x = [x] + \{x\}
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Domain of $f(g(x))$ is NOT simply the domain of $g$; it requires $x \in \text{Domain}(g)$ AND $g(x) \in \text{Domain}(f)$!

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: The range of $f(x) = a\sin x + b\cos x + c$ is $[c - \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}, \; c + \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}]$.

### 2.2 Injective (One-One), Surjective (Onto) & Inverse (Mappings)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **16 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Horizontal line test, monotonicity test for injectivity, codomain matching for surjectivity, and finding function inverses.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{One-One: } f'(x) > 0 \text{ (strictly monotonic)}, \quad \text{Onto: } \text{Range}(f) = \text{Codomain}(f), \quad \text{Bijective } \iff \text{Invertible}
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: A function cannot be invertible unless it is BOTH one-one and onto (bijective).

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: If $f(x)$ is continuous and strictly increasing ($f'(x) > 0$) or strictly decreasing on $\mathbb{R}$, it is always one-one.

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring JEE Mains Pitfalls in Functions 2026 2 questions 3.33% weightage ↓33.4%

### 1. Sign Convention & Vector Inversion Errors
Paper-setters frequently exploit sign confusion in energy and potential differences. Always write the fundamental thermodynamic / vector definition before substituting numerical values.

### 2. Unit System Discrepancies
Molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), SI vs CGS units, and micro/milli/nano multipliers (10^-3, 10^-6, 10^-9) account for over 35% of calculation mistakes in numerical type questions.

### 3. Boundary & Extreme Conditions
In transient circuits or limiting conditions (t=0+, t -> inf, infinite dilution, resonance), always check the asymptotic behavior of inductors, capacitors, and electrolyte mobility.

### 4. Direct Addition Fallacy
Never algebraically add intensive quantities (such as electrode potentials or AC component voltages) without accounting for electron weighting (n1*E1 + n2*E2 = n3*E3) or phasor vector geometry (V_total = sqrt(V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2)).
